title: Gradual Localization of Itinerant Cobalt 3d Electrons in the Pyrochlore Ferromagnetic Metal LuInCo4
authors: Taiki Shiotani, Subaru Yoshimoto, Yoshikazu Tabata, Yusuke Nambu, Katsuki Kinjo, Kazuhiro Nawa, Taku J. Sato, Takeshi Waki, Hiroyuki Nakamura
abstract: We investigated the microscopic magnetic state of the itinerant-electron ferromagnet LuInCo4 with a cobalt pyrochlore lattice by means of powder and single-crystal neutron diffraction measurements. The powder neutron diffraction profiles at zero field are well described by a simple q = 0 collinear ferromagnetic structure with an ordered Co moment of 0.9 uB. Single-crystal neutron diffraction experiments further suggest the absence of both antiferromagnetic order and long-period helical magnetic modulation. In addition, diffuse magnetic scattering was observed around q = 0, with its intensity distribution gradually broadened in reciprocal space upon cooling. Based on these observations, we propose a possible microscopic origin of the low-temperature metamagnetic transition in terms of a ferromagnetic instability enhanced by gradual localization of the itinerant Co-3d electrons. These results suggest that LuInCo4 provides a model system for investigating the interplay between electron localization and itinerant-electron ferromagnetism in cobalt-based metallic pyrochlore compounds.
summary: This work uses neutron diffraction on LuInCo4 to characterize its magnetic state, confirming a collinear ferromagnetism. Key findings include evidence for a gradual localization of Co-3d electrons upon cooling, which the authors propose enhances the residual ferromagnetic instability. This mechanism is suggested to explain the unusual, anisotropic metamagnetic transition observed at low temperatures.
main_problem: The study investigates the microscopic magnetic state and the origin of the low-temperature metamagnetic transition in the itinerant-electron ferromagnet LuInCo4.
main_result: The magnetic structure is confirmed to be a collinear ferromagnet, and the metamagnetic transition is proposed to arise from a ferromagnetic instability enhanced by the gradual localization of itinerant Co-3d electrons.
method: The research employed powder and single-crystal neutron diffraction measurements, supplemented by analysis of diffuse magnetic scattering intensity evolution.
model_or_system: The physical system is LuInCo4, a cobalt-based metallic pyrochlore compound exhibiting itinerant-electron ferromagnetism. The focus is on the interplay between electron localization and magnetic ordering in this lattice structure.
key_observables: Ordered Co magnetic moment ($\mu_{	ext{Co}}$), diffuse magnetic scattering intensity evolution, and the critical field ($H_m$) dependence on temperature and field direction.
important_parameters: The ordered moment is found to be around $0.9 \ \mu_{	ext{B}}$ at zero field, and the metamagnetic transition is observed below 100 K.
main_assumptions: The analysis assumes that the observed diffuse scattering broadening is indicative of a gradual localization of the Co-3d electron character, which enhances the magnetic instability.
figures_summary: Figures show PND profiles confirming a $\mathbf{q}=0$ collinear ferromagnetism, while diffuse scattering maps illustrate the temperature-dependent broadening of intensity towards higher q-space regions.
paper_structure: The paper proceeds by first establishing the basic magnetic structure using zero-field neutron diffraction, then analyzing the temperature dependence of the magnetic moments and diffuse scattering to pinpoint the mechanism (electron localization), and finally connecting this mechanism to the anomalous metamagnetic transition.
why_interesting: The concept of electron localization driving a magnetic transition is central to strongly correlated electron physics, providing a concrete experimental platform to test theories of itinerant magnetism beyond simple mean-field models.
